faults.quote: The network is the same six routes as in FY2023, with the same number of flights on each. Here's an exhibit: Larkspur Air — Results by route, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($ millions unless noted).
faults.why: The candidate asked for departures and average fare for FY2023 vs FY2025. Flights were answered, but average fare got no release, refusal or deferral, and Exhibit 1 has no fares.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: On Hub–Port Avery, revenue fell from $46.8M to $32.4M and contribution fell from $13.8M to a $0.6M loss, on 3,000 flights a year.
faults.why: This repeats an Exhibit 1 line already on screen, appended to an answer about Port Avery's fare, which it doesn't answer.

faults.quote: I'm putting up an exhibit: Hub–Lakeport — Economics of one one-way flight, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($).
faults.why: The candidate asked about the load-factor trend and when the fare started dropping. Exhibit 2 shows only FY2023 vs FY2025 values, so the timing ask (competitor_entry: early FY2024) got no word until the candidate asked again.

faults.quote: Earlier you said Lakeport was around $160 in FY2023 after applying a 33% decline to $120. Which base did you apply the 33% to?
faults.why: In t9 the candidate had already replaced the $160 estimate with the exhibit's figure, $200 to $120, down 40%.

The candidate claimed Port Avery is the structurally worse route and said to focus there first. Port Avery actually loses about $200 per flight against Lakeport's $600. The claim went unprobed, and the blanket approval reads as endorsing it.

faults.quote: Variable cost on the new routes is estimated at $9,200 per flight, across 5,000 flights a year that would use the aircraft time freed by exiting Hub–Lakeport (2,000 flights) and Hub–Port Avery (3,000 flights).
faults.why: The candidate asked how many flights a day the entrant runs. This releases the new-routes cost and flights item instead, which is another entity, gated well past the current stage, and hands over the exit-and-redeploy solution. The entrant-flights ask also got no refusal.

faults.quote: Walk me through how you got that figure and why Port Avery's fare erosion is the right number to apply to Lakeport.
faults.why: The $4,800 per flight (an $80 drop × 60 passengers) is correct, and Lakeport's own fare drop is also $80. Challenging it pushed the candidate to disown right math.

faults.quote: Walk me through how you got that figure
faults.why: 'That figure' dangles. The acknowledgment just mentioned the 40%, so it's unclear which figure is meant.

faults.quote: Air travel demand in Larkspur's cities has been roughly flat.
faults.why: The candidate asked for a demand estimate for the new candidate routes. This line is about Larkspur's existing cities, not the new routes.

faults.quote: New routes typically take 6–12 months to reach their expected load factor, and in the first year the load factor is often around 60%. What do those figures tell you?
faults.why: The candidate applied the entrant's 30% cost-per-seat gap to the $20M of fixed costs, claiming about $6M addressable and $13.8M profit. Leases are locked through 2030 and the logic is conceptually wrong, yet it was never probed or corrected before the close.
